steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a cookie sheet.
Cream sugar and butter together until smooth. Stir in pumpkin puree, egg, chopped walnuts, and vanilla. Stir in flour, baking powder, and salt; mix well to combine.
Drop tablespoonfuls of dough onto the prepared cookie sheet. Bake in the preheated oven until edges are lightly browned and firm, about 15 minutes. Transfer cookies to a wire rack to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Pumpkin Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These cake-like pumpkin cookies are soft, moist, and full of fall flavor. Quick and easy to make with pumpkin puree for a homemade holiday treat.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Pumpkin Cookies

review.reviewBody: I made these cookies (minus the walnuts) and my roommates all thought they were simply the best.

So, because I was reading off my phone screen, I missed the last ingrident which was salt. I know the 'chemistry' of baking depends so much on salt and other low quantity ingredients, I'll have to try again because my version of the cookie, came out kind of flat. I did use butter which was salted in the cookie mix. Other tweaks: 1) Raisins added 2) Pumpkin spice added 3) Frosted with Carmel Icing (also used salted butter to make, so the cookies were definitely not a bust . . . ) Here's the Carmel Icing recipe from my mother-in-law: 1 stick (1/4 pound) of butter 1 cup of brown sugar (better to use light brown but dark OK) 1/2 cup of Evaporated milk 1 lb (pound) box of powdered sugar Combine butter, brown sugar and evaporated milk in a saucepan. Over low heat, bring to a boil and let boil one minute. Take off stove and allow to cool 15 minutes. Add boiled mixture to powdered sugar in a mixing bowl. Allow mixture to set 15 minutes. Mixture should be just soft enough to spread without tearing cake/cookie or have fractured surface appearance. Pro Tip: If too soft and runny, add more powdered sugar; Conversely, if to stiff/dry, add milk sparingly.

I added pumpkin pie spices (2 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp ginger, 1/2 tsp nutmeg, 1/4 tsp cloves) and used gluten-free flour. I can't imagine pumpkin anything without the pumpkin pie spices. I like that they're not too sweet. Just the right amount of sweetness.

I have a gluten and rice allergy so I substituted almond flour for the all purpose. I also added cinnamon, cloves and used maple extract instead of vanilla. Recommend flattening a bit as they hold their shape during baking. Tasted awesome

I omitted the egg since pumpkin is a great egg substitute and gave it the old snickerdoodle treatment in a quarter cup of sugar a tbsp of pie spice and a tbsp of cinnamon. Pretty good, and that's coming from someone who doesn't like pumpkin lol. Very little spreading so sort of make sure it's the size and shape you want. I used a scoop and flattened them out after the sugar roll.
Love these cookies made just as the recipe states. I also make them for my Dad adding 1 tsp. pumpkin pie spice and 1 cup of butterscotch chips. Those are also very tasty. Good solid recipe.

I was looking for a soft pumpkin cookie recipe and this turned out pretty much at the texture/consistency I was looking for. Definitely more muffin-like/chewy than regular cookies as others have mentioned, but that's what I wanted. I doubled the recipe because I wanted to use a full 2-cups of pumpkin (I made my own purée and allotted it in 2-cup increments). I also made several adjustments: I doubled (again) the butter content (for a total of 4 Tbsp), used 3/4 cup brown sugar and 3/4 cup white sugar (so 1.5 total for the doubled recipe), cut the vanilla to 1 tsp., and added 1 tsp of pumpkin pie spice. I eliminated the walnuts. The flavor was good, but very mild. If I make this again, I'll add more pumpkin pie spice and possibly more pumpkin to kick up the flavor. And as others have mentioned, definitely grease the cookie sheet.

Instead of walnuts, I used milk chocolate chips. I love the low fat recipe but I also reduced the sugar just a bit. Just as yummy. I also added a home made pumpkin spice. (1tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ginger, 1/4 tsp nutmeg and 1/8 tsp ground cloves)

these were great with a few adjustments! Here's what i did: add 1 1/2 tsp. pumkin pie spice, use 1/2 a cup brown sugar and 1/2 white, i used homemade pumkin puree which was really watery so i added more flour also. they were really good!
I added a little pumpkin pie spice and cinnamon and crushed pecans

I tried this recipe on the fly because I had about a cup of pumpkin puree left over and had the other ingredients immediately on hand (except walnuts). As I was mixing the ingredients together, I noticed that a very stiff dough forms. Instead of making cookies, I made muffins. I added a teaspoon of pumpkin pie spice which really brought the pumpkin flavor through; without the spice, I don't think the pumpkin flavor would be as prominent. The muffins were more like biscuits. My family seems to enjoy them so I think this would make for a delicious breakfast treat. As muffins/biscuits, they taste great microwaved for 15 seconds with a little butter added.

It turned out pretty good. Not a lot of pumpkin flavor, next time I’ll add some pumpkin spice. The only issue I had was getting the one cup of sugar to actually cream with only two tablespoons of butter. Overall, my wife loves them, and that’s really all that matters!
No flavor! Even added pumpkin pie spice and white chocolate chips. Blah.
Easy to make Great flavor I can add in raisins chocolate chip nuts what ever I'm craving at the time
The recipe and directions are easy to follow to make and enjoy delicious pumpkin cookies. I'm going to make more now. 🙂
Next time I will add pumpkin pie spice and more pumpkin purée.
they are so good, my family loves them. I will be making these again for fall. Such a nice treat to make. Taste just like fall i love these
Really yummy, I did not use walnuts, but I used chocolate chips! It took it to a whole new level! Not a usual texture though like a normal cookie, more spongy and light!👼. Highly recommend!!!
I added chocolate chips and cinnamon glaze. It was easy to make and am awaiting the verdict.
love it
